annotations.title: The Epistle of Christ.
annotations.text: [1] S. Paul and other holy writers of Scriptures did set downe many thinges in writing, by penne, inke, and paper, al which be of the Holy Ghost: but the special and proper booke of Christes truth and Gospel, is not the external writing in those dead creatures, but in the hartes of the faithful, being the proper subiecte of these truthes and graces preached in the new Testament, and the habitacle of the Holy Ghost. In the which booke of faithful mens hartes S. Paul wrote diuers thinges not vttered in any Epistle: as sundrie of the Apostles wrote the Christian religion in the hartes of their hearers onely, and in other material bookes not at all. Whereof S. Irenæus li. 3. c. 4. saith, [2] What and if the Apostles also had left no Scriptures, ought we not to follow the order of the tradition, which they deliuered vnto them to whom they committed the Churches? to the which ordinance many nations of those barbarous people that haue beleeued in Christ, do consent, without letter or inke, hauing saluation written in their hartes, and keeping diligently the tradition of the elders. And S. Hierom, (cont. Io. Hieros. c. 9. ad Pam.) In the Creede of our faith and hope, which being deliuered by tradition from the Apostles, is not written in paper and inke, but in the tables carnal of the hart. And this is the Churches booke also, whereby and wherein she keepeth faithfully al truth written in the hartes of those to whom the Apostles did preach, with the like diligence as she keepeth and preserueth the other booke which is of holy Scriptures, from al corruption of Heretikes and other iniuries.

notes.text: The Apostles wrote the Gospel in mens hartes much more then in paper.

annotations.title: Of our selues.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> This maketh first against the Heretikes called Pelagians, that hold our meritorious actions or cogitations to be of free wil onely, and not of Gods special grace. Secondly against the Protestantes, who on the contrarie side referre al to God, and take away mans freedom and proper motion in his thoughtes and doings: the Apostle confessing our good cogitations to be our owne, but not as comming of our selues, but of God.

notes.text: Gods grace & free will both must concurre.

annotations.title: The letter killeth.
annotations.text: ◦ As the letter of the old Law not truely vnderstood, nor referred to Christ, commaunding and not giuing grace and spirit to fulfil that which was commaunded, did by occasion kill the carnal Iew: so the letter of the new Testament not truely taken nor expounded by the spirit of Christ (which is onely in his Church) killeth the soule of the Heretike: who also being carnal and void of spirit, gaineth nothing by the external precepts or good lessons of the Scriptures, but rather taketh hurt by the same. See S. Augustine to. 10. Ser. 70 & 100 de tempore. & li. de Sp. & lit. c. 5. 6. & seq.

notes.text: The letter killeth both Iew and Heretike.

annotations.title: Much more.
annotations.text: ◦ The preeminence of the new Testament and of the priesthod or Ministerie thereof before the old, is, that the new, by al her Sacraments and Priests as ministers immediate of grace and remission of sinnes, doth so ex opere operato giue the spirit of life and charitie into the hartes of the faithful, as the old did giue the letter or external act of the Law.

notes.text: The preeminence of the new Testament, Sacraments, &c.

annotations.title: The self same vele.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> As the Iewes reading the old Testament, by reason of their blindnes (which God for the punishment of their incredulitie suffereth to remaine as a couer vpon their eies and hartes) can not see Christ in the Scriptures which they daily heare read in their Synagogs, but shal, when they beleeue in him and haue the couer remoued, perceiue al to be most plainely done and spoken of him in their law & Scriptures: euen so Heretikes hauing (as S. Augustine <mn>[2]</mn> noteth) a farre greater couer of blindnes and incredulitie ouer their hartes in respect of the Catholike Church which they impugne, then the Iewes haue concerning Christ, can not see, though they read or heare the Scriptures read neuer so much, the maruelous euidence of the Catholike Church and truth in al pointes: but when they shal returne againe to the obedience of the same Church, they shal finde the Scriptures most cleere for her and her doctrine, and shal wonder at their former blindnes.

notes.text: The heretikes more blinde in not seing the Church, then the Iewes in not seing Christ.

annotations.title: Libertie.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> The Spirit and grace of God in the new Testament dischargeth vs of the bondage of the Law and sinne, but is not a warrant to vs of fleshly licence, as S. Peter writeth: <mn>[2]</mn>nor dischargeth Christians of their obedience to order, law, and power of Magistrates spiritual or temporal, as some Heretikes of these daies do seditiously teach.
